CrossTalk style Multiplayer drawing games scene. each game can be its own component/preset.
- Competitive Scribble. Everyone gets the same canvas. everyone gets assigned a color, cursor appears as a large pencil with a very tiny tip, brush size is a few pixels. players have n seconds to cover as much of the canvas as possible. players can draw over eachother. randomly a pink rubber eraser will blow across the screen and clear some pixels. after the timer elapses we count up the pixels per user, then declare a winner.
-  Collaborative Scribble. Everyone gets the same canvas. Everyone has a different colored brush. Draw together in real time. Periodically the game gives prompts: "Make a monster" "Add something that flies" "Turn it into a spaceship"
- Draw in the Dark. Shared canvas, entirely covered by a fog of darkness except for a flashlight cookie around the cursor/pen. You have to draw something without seeing the whole canvas, When time expires, the lights come on.
-  Draw the Path. A little creature/vehicle needs to get from A → B. Players draw the path it should follow. Then: RUN! The physics engine follows the drawing. If you draw a ramp, the vehicle jumps. If you draw a loop, it loops. If you draw a terrible path, everyone watches the poor creature die. Then players get to modify the path and try again.
- Draw Battle. Players receive the same mad-lobs style prompt. They have 60 seconds. But there are weird constraints: (ex. Draw a cat without lifting your brush. Draw a house using exactly 12 strokes. Draw a monster using only circles. Draw something recognizable using only straight lines.) Then everyone votes.
- Saboteur. One player is secretly the Saboteur. Everyone gets: "Draw a castle." The saboteur gets: "Make the castle subtly look like a spaceship." Nobody knows who the saboteur is. At the end, everyone votes: WHO WAS THE SABOTEUR?
- Radiance drawing. radiance cascades and users can draw in emitting lines and occluding lines
